CC-01.title: Person and episode identity
CC-01.semantics: Stable synthetic PersonId; distinct ReferralId, EncounterId, AdmissionId, TransferId. Typed one-to-many relationships (Person to multiple ServiceEpisodes). Recycled ECS generation/indices are isolated from longitudinal clinical identities.

CC-02.title: Transfer lifecycle
CC-02.semantics: Ten explicit states: Requested, Offered, Reserved, Departing, InTransit, Arrived, HandoverComplete, Rejected, Cancelled, Expired. TransferOperationId with idempotent logical effects. Originating resources retained until authoritative HandoverComplete event.

CC-03.title: Resource bundle allocation and safe interruption
CC-03.semantics: Explicit team/room/equipment bundles. Staged sequential claims with rollback on partial failure; AllOf/AnyOf are event joins, not atomic resource allocators. Contention, expiry, and preemption policies without silent eviction.

CC-04.title: Independent clinical progression
CC-04.semantics: Patient clinical state evolves independently while waiting, boarding, or traveling. Discrete competing risks with deterministic tie-breaking. Reassessment does not resample unrelated clocks.

CC-05.title: Effective capacity and calendars
CC-05.semantics: Eight states: Physical, Equipped, Staffed, Open, Reserved, Occupied, Cleaning, Unavailable. Maintenance, turnover, and operational calendars without silent eviction of active clinical care.

CC-06.title: Virtual clocks and policy isolation
CC-06.semantics: Single virtual clock with explicit integer Tick units. Strict isolation between triage urgency, operational priority, target clock thresholds, and interruption eligibility. Decision policies cannot observe latent future outcomes.

CC-07.title: Reproducible composition
CC-07.semantics: Hierarchical random stream namespaces (RootRng, PersonStream, ModuleStream, WorkerStream). Deterministic event ordering and cross-worker equivalence (1, 2, 4 worker threads produce byte-identical or trace-identical results).

CC-08.title: Observation and evaluation
CC-08.semantics: Latent state vs observed state distinction. Explicit handling of delays, missingness, interval/right censoring. Separate ledgers for activity, clinical outcomes, financial costs, and equity.
